RPE is "rate of perceived exertion," a 1 to 10 score for how hard a set felt. A 10 means you couldn't have done another rep, a 9 means one rep left in the tank, an 8 means two left, and so on.

It's useful because it lets you match the effort to the day. Some days a weight moves fast and some days it grinds, and RPE keeps you honest on both. Most working sets land around 7 to 9. It gets more accurate the more you practice judging "how many reps did I have left?"

If you want, tell me what you're working on and I'll show you where it fits.
